notes: Thanksgiving swapped for Christmas; 'Werden die noch größer?' keeps both readings (bigger sizes / still growing). The lady is the wife puppet as a customer, the stock boy is the young guy in an apron.
title: Noch größer?

lines.text: Als ich für Weihnachten einen Truthahn holen wollte, habe ich dieses Juwel aufgeschnappt.
Eine Frau wühlte in den gefrorenen Truthähnen, fand aber keinen, der groß genug für ihre Familie war.
Werden die noch größer?
Nein, gnädige Frau, die sind tot.

notes: Dialogue kept word for word; 'I called my wife at work' became a one-line narrator setup. Cross-cut phone call: husband at home, wife at her office desk.
title: How About Now?

lines.text: A man calls his wife at work.
Do you ever get a shooting pain across your body, like someone's got a voodoo doll of you and they're stabbing it?
No.
How about now?

notes: Line-by-line translation; 'How about now?' becomes the short 'А сейчас?'. Cross-cut phone call: husband at home, wife at work.
title: А сейчас?

lines.text: Мужик звонит жене на работу.
У тебя бывает такая стреляющая боль по всему телу, как будто у кого-то есть твоя кукла вуду и он её протыкает?
Нет.
А сейчас?

notes: Line-by-line translation; 'How about now?' becomes 'Und jetzt?'. Cross-cut phone call: husband at home, wife at work.
title: Und jetzt?

lines.text: Ein Mann ruft seine Frau bei der Arbeit an.
Hast du manchmal einen stechenden Schmerz im ganzen Körper, als hätte jemand eine Voodoo-Puppe von dir und würde hineinstechen?
Nein.
Und jetzt?

notes: Both lines kept as written. The salesman stands in an empty kitchen and lays a brochure on the table, so the picture backs up the reveal.
title: Door to Door

lines.text: I used to sell security alarms door to door, and I was really good at it.
If no one was home, I would just leave a brochure on the kitchen table.

notes: Literal translation; 'door to door' becomes 'по квартирам'. The salesman lays a brochure on someone's kitchen table.
title: Сигнализация

lines.text: Раньше я продавал охранную сигнализацию по квартирам, и у меня это отлично получалось.
Если никого не было дома, я просто оставлял буклет на кухонном столе.

notes: Literal translation; 'door to door' becomes 'an der Haustür'. The salesman lays a brochure on someone's kitchen table.
title: Alarmanlagen

lines.text: Früher habe ich Alarmanlagen an der Haustür verkauft, und ich war richtig gut darin.
Wenn niemand zu Hause war, habe ich einfach eine Broschüre auf dem Küchentisch liegen lassen.

notes: All lines kept; the dad's answer split into two lines. The son is a small boy (vovochka as a child, not named); the dad has a red nose and a bottle so the reveal is backed by the picture. Park with trees.
title: Four Trees

lines.text: Dad, what's an alcoholic?
Do you see those four trees?
Well, an alcoholic would see eight.
But Dad, I only see two.

notes: Literal translation, every line and number kept. Small son, tipsy dad with red nose and bottle, park with trees.
title: Четыре дерева

lines.text: Пап, а кто такой алкоголик?
Видишь вон те четыре дерева?
Так вот, алкоголик увидел бы восемь.
Но пап, я вижу только два.

notes: Literal translation, every line and number kept. Small son, tipsy dad with red nose and bottle, park with trees.
title: Vier Bäume

lines.text: Papa, was ist ein Alkoholiker?
Siehst du die vier Bäume da?
Ein Alkoholiker würde acht sehen.
Aber Papa, ich sehe nur zwei.

notes: Three lines kept word for word; no narrator needed.
title: Hi Pregnant

lines.text: I'm pregnant.
Hi Pregnant, I'm Dad.
No you're not.

notes: The English dad-joke formula is rebuilt on the familiar Russian pattern 'Я устал. — Очень приятно, Устал, а я…' (short adjective taken as a name), so 'Беременна' works as a name; the punch 'Нет, не папа' keeps the paternity denial.
title: Очень приятно

lines.text: Я беременна.
Очень приятно, Беременна, а я папа.
Нет, не папа.

notes: German knows the Papa-Witz 'Hallo Hunger, ich bin Papa'; one short narrator line sets up that the husband never misses one, then the three lines are translated directly.
title: Hallo Schwanger

lines.text: Ihr Mann lässt keinen Papa-Witz aus.
Ich bin schwanger.
Hallo Schwanger, ich bin Papa.
Nein, bist du nicht.

notes: The man's two lines kept; only 'waaaay' written as 'way' for TTS and 'who's' fixed to 'whose'. The nurse stays on screen silent, since the questions are what she always asks.
title: Personal Questions

lines.text: I was going to donate blood today, but they always ask way too many personal questions.
Like, whose blood is this, and where did you get it?

notes: Literal translation; the two questions kept as the punch. Nurse on screen silent.
title: Личные вопросы

lines.text: Я сегодня собирался сдать кровь, но там всегда задают слишком много личных вопросов.
Например, чья это кровь и где вы её взяли?

notes: Literal translation; the two questions kept as the punch. Nurse on screen silent.
title: Persönliche Fragen

lines.text: Ich wollte heute Blut spenden, aber die stellen immer viel zu viele persönliche Fragen.
Zum Beispiel: Wessen Blut ist das, und wo haben Sie das her?

notes: Both lines kept as written. The parents are on screen silent (mother and father) beside the glum son; the twin has no free double of paren, and the joke does not need him seen.
title: My Twin Brother

lines.text: I finally realized my parents favored my twin brother.
It hit me when they asked me to blow up balloons for his surprise birthday party.

notes: Literal translation; 'favored' as 'любили больше'. Parents on screen silent.
title: Брат-близнец

lines.text: Я наконец понял, что родители любили моего брата-близнеца больше.
Дошло, когда они попросили меня надуть шарики для его дня рождения-сюрприза.

notes: Literal translation. Parents on screen silent.
title: Mein Zwillingsbruder

lines.text: Endlich habe ich gemerkt, dass meine Eltern meinen Zwillingsbruder bevorzugen.
Mir wurde es klar, als sie mich baten, Luftballons für seine Überraschungs-Geburtstagsparty aufzublasen.

notes: All dialogue kept as written; the reported order became the guy's own line, narration kept with only light trimming. The waitress is the girl puppet in an apron (not the male barman); the other diner is a second man.
title: The Last Bowl

lines.text: A guy sits down in a diner.
A bowl of hot chili, please.
Sorry, but the guy next to you got the last bowl.
He looks over and sees that the guy's finished his meal, but the bowl of chili is still full.
Are you going to eat that chili?
No. Help yourself.
He slides the bowl of chili over and starts to eat.
When he gets about halfway down, his spoon hits something.
He looks down, sees a dead mouse and immediately pukes all the chili back into the bowl.
Yeah, that's about as far as I got, too.
